# Who holds vehicle data in the UK {#sec-data-landscape}

Information about vehicles in the UK is collected by several government
bodies, each for its own administrative purpose. Knowing who collects what, and
why, explains much of what is in the CARS data and what is missing from it.

## The Department for Transport and its agencies

The Department for Transport (DfT) is responsible for transport policy. Two
of its executive agencies hold the records that CARS draws on, and DfT itself
publishes official statistics built from them.

### Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA)

The DVLA, based in Swansea, keeps the **register of vehicles** (and of
drivers) for Great Britain, and since 2014 for Northern Ireland as well. Every
vehicle used on public roads must be registered. The register records the
vehicle's identity and specification, its registered keeper, and its tax
status. The DVLA:

- issues the **registration number** (@sec-number-plates) and the **V5C
  registration certificate** ("logbook"), reissued whenever the keeper or a key
  detail changes;
- collects **vehicle excise duty** (vehicle tax), whose rates depend on CO~2~
  emissions, fuel and age, which is why the register records these;
- records vehicles declared off the road (**SORN**), exported, or scrapped
  (@sec-lifecycle).

The keeper's name and address are personal data and are not published. The
DVLA publishes the vehicle details for any registration number through the
**Vehicle Enquiry Service (VES)**, used by the public to check a vehicle's tax
and MOT status. CARS uses the VES programming interface (API) to add DVLA
details to each vehicle (@sec-sources-linkage).

### Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA)

The DVSA sets and enforces vehicle testing standards in Great Britain. It runs
the **MOT scheme** (@sec-mot-test) and the annual test for heavy vehicles, and
holds the record of every MOT test. It publishes MOT data in two ways that CARS
uses:

- the **anonymised MOT test data**: every test, with the test date, result,
  odometer reading, test class and postcode area of the testing station, but
  without the registration number;
- the **MOT history API**, including a bulk download: every registered
  vehicle, with its registration number, make, model, fuel and dates, and the
  history of its MOT tests (but no location).

### Driver & Vehicle Agency, Northern Ireland (DVA)

Vehicle testing in Northern Ireland is run separately, by the DVA. Its tests
reach the DVSA datasets, but Northern Ireland differs from Great Britain in
ways that show in the data: the first test is at four years, tests are carried
out at government test centres, and the test class is not supplied
(@sec-mot-test).

## Official statistics

DfT publishes several statistical series about vehicles and their use. They
are the natural benchmarks for the CARS data, and CARS uses some of them
directly.

| Series | What it covers | How it relates to CARS |
|---|---|---|
| [Vehicle licensing statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/vehicles-statistics) | Counts of licensed and SORN vehicles from the DVLA register, by body type, make, model, fuel, age and area (the VEH tables) | CARS uses DfT's make and model names (VEH0220, VEH0124) and compares its vehicle counts with DfT's (@sec-data-quality) |
| [Road traffic statistics](https://roadtraffic.dft.gov.uk/) | Vehicle miles travelled on roads, estimated from traffic counts | Measures traffic on the roads of an area, whoever drives it; CARS measures the distance driven by vehicles tested in an area, wherever it is driven |
| [National Travel Survey](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/national-travel-survey-statistics) (NTS) | A household survey of how people travel in England, including car mileage | Survey-based and England only, but links travel to people and households |
| Anonymised MOT data | Test-level MOT results, published since 2010 | One of the CARS sources (@sec-sources-linkage) |

Other sources often used alongside vehicle data:

- **The Census** (ONS, NRS and NISRA) records the number of cars or vans
  available to each household, for small areas.
- **SMMT** (the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders) publishes new
  vehicle registrations by make, model and fuel.

## Open data and the Open Government Licence

The three sources CARS combines are published under the
[Open Government Licence](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/)
(OGL). The OGL allows anyone to copy, adapt, combine and republish the
information, including commercially, provided the source is acknowledged.
Because each source may be used and republished, so may the combination, and
the CARS data products are released on the same basis (@sec-data-products).

The difficulty with these sources has never been access. It is that they are
very large, structured for administration rather than analysis, and not
linked to each other. The bulk MOT history download alone is over 400 GB of
compressed JSON files. CARS does the linking and restructuring so that others
do not have to.
